motion.name: console-boot
motion.value: opacity 0->1, translateY(6px)->0, 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), staggered 50ms per panel
motion.purpose: The dashboard's one signature entrance moment: header then panels light up in a single coordinated cascade, never scattered per-element fades.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Filled phosphor-accent action button, used sparingly against the mostly text-button panel headers.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #39ff6a; color: #0a0f0d; border: 1px solid #39ff6a; border-radius: 3px; padding: 6px 14px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 500; transition: background 0.15s ease, transform 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #5fe08c; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #39ff6a; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Status Tag
components.description: Priority/status tag: tinted background + solid text, never outline-only. Shown here in its danger (high priority / overdue) variant.
components.css: .ds-tag { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 2px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; } .ds-tag-danger { background: rgba(239,68,68,0.16); color: #fca5a5; } .ds-tag-warn { background: rgba(255,171,74,0.16); color: #ffab4a; } .ds-tag-success { background: rgba(57,255,106,0.16); color: #39ff6a; }

components.name: Console Panel
components.description: The base dashboard panel: flat, hairline-bordered, no shadow. Each panel's internal content differs (table/list/grid) but the shell is shared.

components.css: .ds-panel { background: #101613; border: 1px solid #232f29; border-radius: 4px; padding: 16px; } .ds-panel__header { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; margin-bottom: 12px; } .ds-panel__header h2 { margin: 0; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.9375rem; font-weight: 600; color: #eaf6ea; } .ds-panel__link { background: none; border: none; color: #39ff6a; font-size: 0.8125rem; cursor: pointer; }

components.name: Nav Rail Item
components.description: A single nav-rail row in its active state: hairline-tinted background plus a 3px phosphor indicator bar on the leading edge.
components.css: .ds-nav-item { position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 8px 16px; color: #7fa08d; text-decoration: none; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; } .ds-nav-item--active { color: #eaf6ea; background: rgba(57,255,106,0.08); font-weight: 500; } .ds-nav-item__indicator { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 50%; width: 3px; height: 60%; background: #39ff6a; transform: translateY(-50%); box-shadow: 0 0 8px rgba(57,255,106,0.25); }

components.name: Command Dock
components.description: The system's signature persistent bottom strip: current section, a ⌘K command trigger, and a live ticking mono clock.

components.css: .ds-dock { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; height: 44px; padding: 0 16px; background: #101613; border-top: 1px solid #232f29; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; color: #7fa08d; } .ds-dock__section { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; color: #eaf6ea; } .ds-dock__dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 999px; background: #39ff6a; box-shadow: 0 0 6px rgba(57,255,106,0.25); } .ds-dock__trigger { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: none; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 3px; padding: 2px 12px; color: #7fa08d; cursor: pointer; } .ds-dock__trigger:hover { color: #eaf6ea; border-color: #34483f; }

narrative.overview: DevCenter reads as a real instrument console, not another rounded-card SaaS dashboard. The product's own name — Command Center — is taken literally: a developer's daily tasks, notes, projects and tools surface as telemetry on a dim, glowing desk, the way an operator reads status off a panel rather than scrolling a feed. Density and precision come first; ornament does not. Dark ("console") is the native, default scheme — a room lit mostly by its own panels. Light ("daylight desk") is a genuine second rendition, not an inverted palette: brushed-steel panels on warm paper under daylight, ink readouts instead of glowing phosphor. Both share the same structure, radii, spacing and component language; only the material and glow change.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black or warm-paper ground, never the default cool slate/gray SaaS neutral.
Squared, hairline-bordered panels — no soft rounded shadow cards.
Monospace reserved strictly for numerals, timestamps, and durations.
One accent (phosphor green) carries state; amber and red are reserved for warning/overdue signals only, never decoration.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Phosphor green is the only chromatic accent. Amber and red exist solely as status signals and are never used decoratively.

rules.name: The Two Text Tiers Rule
rules.body: Any string a person needs to actually read uses readout-phosphor or readout-phosphor-dim, never the dimmest gray tier — that is reserved for non-text decoration only.

rules.name: The Measurement-Only Mono Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono is used exclusively for numerals, clocks, dates and durations — never as a generic technical-looking costume over prose.

rules.name: The Border-Or-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A static panel declares elevation with a hairline border. A shadow is reserved for things that are genuinely floating above the page — never both on the same element.

dos: Do use IBM Plex Mono + font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums for any count, clock, date or duration.
Do give every dashboard panel a materially different internal structure suited to its content — not a repeated card shell.
Do reserve amber/red strictly for warning/overdue/high-priority signal, never as decoration.
Do declare elevation with a border on static panels; reserve shadow for genuinely floating overlays.
donts: Don't add a kicker/eyebrow label above any heading.
Don't combine a hairline border with an ambient drop shadow on the same static panel (the "ghost card").
Don't use the dimmest neutral tier for any string a person needs to read.
Don't animate width/height/padding/margin for state changes; use transform/opacity.
